cost_statement:
SURETY REAL LANE, M6 (row M519): what this run can cost, before anything starts.
A guess, not a promise (E156 Q5): perhaps 10 to 18 USD. V1 (the same brief, no Designer) was 8.61 USD; a Designer session on Opus of several turns adds perhaps 1 to 4 USD per target per session, and the review at Alpha is a second Designer session.
  The qualification attempts, once per run directory and per model: Opus with the continuation canary, Sonnet; under 0.50 USD (M519 pays them; M535 in the same run directory reuses them).
At most: each run (a session is one run) is bounded by 2000000 billable tokens, each Designer session by 3000000; the project's day limit of 40 USD in estimates stops it earlier (a UTC day), and its day bound on unknown usage is 4000000 tokens. The widenings are yours to confirm (policy_widening). The only hard maximum is your subscription's own usage limits.
An estimate, not a cap and not an authorization. Nothing paid starts before your qualification_approval and trust_activation.

deltas.owner_words: The start-up failure card has no logo and no "Reload the page" button. The design puts the on_light logo (on_dark in the dark theme) at the top of the card, with a Reload button under the message. The build put those two logos in a page footer instead, and the design has no logo in the footer. The asset checks R8.17 and R8.18 pass only because they compare the files' bytes, not where the logos are shown. Fix: move the <picture> into the #startup-error card and add the Reload button. findings.what: Design readiness deadlock: the design's consolidated spec change (scr_01M56E0GBWEPD25ZHEGXQYZ6XM) added R6.1, R7.1 and R8.20, design criteria of kind human, as ordinary criteria; designReadiness (design/approval.ts ~1018) requires every added criterion covered by a check of the effective version (stricter than D7 §7.5); the Verifier rightly wrote no check for human-judged criteria and deferred them to stage 4 (prerequisite), which is itself held design_pending: the design stays approved with ready_at null, stages 3 and 4 held, nothing in flight and no question naming the cause (design_due offers only open/waive/policy_off/later). Observed 03:17 UTC, stalled since 02:44.

The rerun of m6w_design (SURETY_REAL_RERUN=m6w_design at 292e11e, 06:38 UTC) was refused before any engine started: the harness's leftovers check (checks-journey.mjs leftovers/refuseLeftovers, evenIfPaused because the step resumes the project) counted stage 3 and stage 4's stage_build items (wi_01M56CC1ZRBKYD2HMNXY0G286C, wi_01M56CC1ZSESC8WJN99KVPM0KW; eligible, no run ever) as work of an earlier attempt that could be dispatched. They are held by the engine's computed design_pending blocker, which leftovers() does not read (it reads only dispatch_hold and the chain limit), so its own stated rule ('an eligible item not held') is not what it checks. Their release is the design step's own purpose. A harness defect of the M6 lane; no tokens spent.

After the rerun of m6w_design passed (07:00 UTC), judge (c) halted the run: 'the combined approval is in the per-act record'. recordActs on a rerun reads storeActs from the rerun's own start (sinceSeq = maxSeq at the rerun, step-starts.json overwritten to 06:56:45) and replaces the step's acts, so the first attempt's acts of the same step (design_due open 02:18, correction approvals, finding dispositions, designer_feedback, preview_inspection 02:38, combined_approval 02:39, all in the store and in driver-acts.jsonl) are absent from acts-M519.json; only qualify_adapter and preview_inspection of the rerun are recorded. A harness defect of the M6 lane's rerun; no tokens spent by it.

Confirming the review's design_verdicts (3 labs, deltas) filed 23 findings (one per implementation delta and lab), each linked to criterion R8.19 and check design-asset-favicon, whatever the delta concerns (the start-up card, input-error wording, the Run button label, the scene grid, the skip link, scene markers, a hint). Their finding_disposition 'fix' would hold the gates only until design-asset-favicon passes, a check unrelated to the defect that already passes, so a fix would be resolved by unrelated evidence; correct_check would name the same unrelated check. Also the design-kind recommendations marked 'both' were filed as implementation defects. The driver answered accept on all 23 (recorded, no gate hold); the defects stay recorded for a later run.
